source.original_text: Let P be a probability law on X×ℝ, with its actual input marginal Pₓ. Let K:W×X→ℝ be a scalar feature, and assume the actual response coordinate belongs to L²(P). Choose N>0 and two indexed parameter configurations w₀,w₁ of length N. Assume only their selected feature functions K(wₐʲ,·) belong to L²(Pₓ), for a=0,1 and every index j. Let ρ₀ and ρ₁ be their literal equally weighted Dirac empirical measures, retaining repeated indices. Define fρ(x)=∫K(w,x) dρ(w), F(ρ)=∫(fρ(x)−y)² dP(x,y), and V(w)=2∫(fρ₀(x)−y)K(w,x) dP(x,y). Every mixture (1−t)ρ₀+tρ₁ for 0≤t≤1 is a probability with integrable squared loss. V is integrable under both empirical laws, and the actual scalar risk along the mixture has right derivative ∫V dρ₁−∫V dρ₀ at zero.

theorem result
    {W X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace W] [MeasurableSingletonClass W] [MeasurableSpace X]
    (P : Measure (X × ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (K : W → X → ℝ)
    (hlabel : MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => z.2) 2 P)
    {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (w0 w1 : Fin N → W)
    (hfeature0 : ∀ j, MemLp (K (w0 j)) 2 (P.map Prod.fst))
    (hfeature1 : ∀ j, MemLp (K (w1 j)) 2 (P.map Prod.fst)) :
    let rho0 : Measure W := (N : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ • ∑ j, Measure.dirac (w0 j)
    let rho1 : Measure W := (N : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ • ∑ j, Measure.dirac (w1 j)
    let curve : ℝ → Measure W := fun t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - t) • rho0 + ENNReal.ofReal t • rho1
    let predictor : Measure W → X → ℝ := fun law x => ∫ q, K q x ∂law
    let risk : Measure W → ℝ := fun law => ∫ z, (predictor law z.1 - z.2) ^ 2 ∂P
    let potential : W → ℝ := fun q =>
      2 * ∫ z, (predictor rho0 z.1 - z.2) * K q z.1 ∂P
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧
      Integrable (fun z : X × ℝ => (predictor (curve t) z.1 - z.2) ^ 2) P) ∧
    Integrable potential rho0 ∧ Integrable potential rho1 ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => risk (curve t))
      ((∫ q, potential q ∂rho1) - (∫ q, potential q ∂rho0))
      (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) 0

blind_reconstruction.text: For every measurable spaces W and X, with measurable singletons in W, every joint probability measure P on X times R, every kernel K:W->X->R, and a supplied L2(P) membership witness for the actual response z->z.2, let N be any natural number with N>0 and w0,w1:Fin N->W any two indexed particle families. Assume for each j:Fin N that K(w0(j)) and K(w1(j)) belong to L2(PX), where PX=P.map Prod.fst. These supplied memberships mean almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm under the indicated actual measures. Use the following fixed definitions. Set PX=P.map Prod.fst, the actual first-coordinate marginal. Define rho0=(N:nonnegative_extended_reals)^(-1) times sum_{j:Fin N} dirac(w0(j)) and rho1=(N:nonnegative_extended_reals)^(-1) times sum_{j:Fin N} dirac(w1(j)). For every real t define the actual positive measure curve(t)=ofReal(1-t) times rho0 + ofReal(t) times rho1, where ofReal(r) embeds max(r,0) into the nonnegative extended reals. Define predictor(law,x)=integral_W K(q,x) dlaw(q) for every measure law on W, and risk(law)=integral_{X times R}(predictor(law,z.1)-z.2)^2 dP(z). Define one potential(q)=2*integral_{X times R}(predictor(rho0,z.1)-z.2)*K(q,z.1) dP(z). Abbreviate D=integral_W potential(q) drho1(q)-integral_W potential(q) drho0(q). Every integral is a literal real Bochner integral on the full displayed space with the indicated measure. Then all four outer conclusions hold: (1) For every t in the closed interval [0,1], curve(t) is a probability measure and z->(predictor(curve(t),z.1)-z.2)^2 is genuinely integrable under P. (2) potential is genuinely integrable under rho0. (3) potential is genuinely integrable under rho1. (4) The real function t->risk(curve(t)) has derivative D within [0,1] at its endpoint 0, including its actual value at 0. There are exactly N indices at each endpoint, without a distinctness condition. Repeated particle values, including overlaps between the two families, accumulate their masses. The segment is supported on the finite union of the endpoint particle values. On [0,1] the coefficients are exactly 1-t and t; curve(0)=rho0 and curve(1)=rho1. Each endpoint predictor is the pointwise arithmetic average of its N sampled raw features, and prediction along this finite segment is their affine interpolation. The derivative is the right-hand derivative relative to the closed interval and uses risk(curve(0))=risk(rho0); it is not an unrestricted two-sided derivative of the clipped extension. The response is the actual second coordinate of P, with no independence or product decomposition assumed. Supplied label and sampled-feature L2 memberships yield the displayed squared-loss and endpoint potential integrability conclusions. No uniform feature norm bound is supplied. Only sampled slices carry feature membership assumptions; no global measurability or L2 assumption on the whole kernel is imposed. For q in the finite endpoint support, the inner potential integrand is genuinely P-integrable by these sampled L2 assumptions. For q outside that support, no such integrability is asserted, so the formula defining potential retains its totalized real-integral meaning there. Potential integrability under the two empirical laws and the derivative statement do not give a genuine global first variation at arbitrary off-support locations or under arbitrary parameter laws. Both scalar integrals in D use the same rho0-anchored potential, with rho1 minus rho0 direction; this is not an integral against positive or truncated subtraction of measures. The risk is the unhalved integrated squared residual, so potential has literal factor 2. The full conclusion has the segment assertion, two endpoint scalar integrability assertions, and the endpoint derivative; no quantitative remainder budget is part of it.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticFeatureRisk

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal InnerProductSpace
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticFeatureRisk

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.JointEmpiricalSegmentRisk

theorem joint_empirical_probability_segment_derivative
    {W X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace W] [MeasurableSingletonClass W] [MeasurableSpace X]
    (P : Measure (X × ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (K : W → X → ℝ)
    (hlabel : MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => z.2) 2 P)
    {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (w0 w1 : Fin N → W)
    (hfeature0 : ∀ j, MemLp (K (w0 j)) 2 (P.map Prod.fst))
    (hfeature1 : ∀ j, MemLp (K (w1 j)) 2 (P.map Prod.fst)) :
    let rho0 : Measure W := (N : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ • ∑ j, Measure.dirac (w0 j)
    let rho1 : Measure W := (N : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ • ∑ j, Measure.dirac (w1 j)
    let curve : ℝ → Measure W := fun t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - t) • rho0 + ENNReal.ofReal t • rho1
    let predictor : Measure W → X → ℝ := fun law x => ∫ q, K q x ∂law
    let risk : Measure W → ℝ := fun law => ∫ z, (predictor law z.1 - z.2) ^ 2 ∂P
    let potential : W → ℝ := fun q =>
      2 * ∫ z, (predictor rho0 z.1 - z.2) * K q z.1 ∂P
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧
      Integrable (fun z : X × ℝ => (predictor (curve t) z.1 - z.2) ^ 2) P) ∧
    Integrable potential rho0 ∧ Integrable potential rho1 ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => risk (curve t))
      ((∫ q, potential q ∂rho1) - (∫ q, potential q ∂rho0))
      (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) 0 := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let rhoOf : (Fin N → W) → Measure W :=
    fun cfg => (N : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ • ∑ j, Measure.dirac (cfg j)
  let curve : ℝ → Measure W := fun t =>
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 - t) • rhoOf w0 + ENNReal.ofReal t • rhoOf w1
  let predictor : Measure W → X → ℝ := fun law x => ∫ q, K q x ∂law
  let risk : Measure W → ℝ := fun law => ∫ z, (predictor law z.1 - z.2) ^ 2 ∂P
  let potential : W → ℝ := fun q =>
    2 * ∫ z, (predictor (rhoOf w0) z.1 - z.2) * K q z.1 ∂P
  change (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧
      Integrable (fun z : X × ℝ => (predictor (curve t) z.1 - z.2) ^ 2) P) ∧
    Integrable potential (rhoOf w0) ∧ Integrable potential (rhoOf w1) ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => risk (curve t))
      ((∫ q, potential q ∂rhoOf w1) - (∫ q, potential q ∂rhoOf w0))
      (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) 0
  have hinv : (N : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ≠ ∞ := by
    apply ENNReal.inv_ne_top.mpr
    exact_mod_cast hN.ne'
  have hInt (cfg : Fin N → W) (g : W → ℝ) : Integrable g (rhoOf cfg) := by
    apply Integrable.smul_measure (c := (N : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹) _ hinv
    exact integrable_finsetSum_measure.mpr (fun j _ => integrable_dirac (by simp))
  have hEval (cfg : Fin N → W) (g : W → ℝ) :
      (∫ q, g q ∂rhoOf cfg) = (N : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ j, g (cfg j) := by
    dsimp only [rhoOf]
    rw [integral_smul_measure,
      integral_finsetSum_measure (fun j _ => integrable_dirac (by simp))]
    simp [smul_eq_mul]
  have hPred (cfg : Fin N → W) (x : X) :
      predictor (rhoOf cfg) x = (N : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ j, K (cfg j) x :=
    hEval cfg (fun q => K q x)
  have hmarg : MeasurePreserving (Prod.fst : X × ℝ → X) P (P.map Prod.fst) :=
    measurable_fst.measurePreserving P
  have hf0 (j : Fin N) : MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => K (w0 j) z.1) 2 P :=
    (hfeature0 j).comp_measurePreserving hmarg
  have hf1 (j : Fin N) : MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => K (w1 j) z.1) 2 P :=
    (hfeature1 j).comp_measurePreserving hmarg
  let mean (cfg : Fin N → W) (hf : ∀ j, MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => K (cfg j) z.1) 2 P) :
      Lp ℝ 2 P := (N : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ j, (hf j).toLp (fun z => K (cfg j) z.1)
  let m0 : Lp ℝ 2 P := mean w0 hf0
  let m1 : Lp ℝ 2 P := mean w1 hf1
  let label : Lp ℝ 2 P := hlabel.toLp (fun z : X × ℝ => z.2)
  have hBase (cfg : Fin N → W) (hf : ∀ j, MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => K (cfg j) z.1) 2 P) :=
    empirical_law_squared_risk_eq_L2_norm P hN cfg
      (fun q z => K q z.1) (fun z => z.2) hf hlabel
  have hMean (cfg : Fin N → W) (hf : ∀ j, MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => K (cfg j) z.1) 2 P) :
      (fun z => mean cfg hf z) =ᵐ[P]
        (fun z : X × ℝ => predictor (rhoOf cfg) z.1) := by
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_smul (N : ℝ)⁻¹ (∑ j, (hf j).toLp (fun z => K (cfg j) z.1)),
      Lp.coeFn_fun_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j => (hf j).toLp (fun z => K (cfg j) z.1)),
      ae_all_iff.2 (fun j => (hf j).coeFn_toLp)] with z hsmul hsum hj
    change (((N : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ j, (hf j).toLp (fun z => K (cfg j) z.1)) z) = _
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hsmul
    rw [hsmul, hsum, hPred]
    congr 1
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => hj j)
  have hResidual : (fun z => (m0 - label) z) =ᵐ[P]
      (fun z : X × ℝ => predictor (rhoOf w0) z.1 - z.2) := by
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_sub m0 label, hMean w0 hf0, hlabel.coeFn_toLp]
      with z hsub hm hy
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at hsub
    rw [hsub, hm, hy]
  have hPotMean (cfg : Fin N → W)
      (hf : ∀ j, MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => K (cfg j) z.1) 2 P) :
      (∫ q, potential q ∂rhoOf cfg) = 2 * ⟪m0 - label, mean cfg hf⟫_ℝ := by
    have hpot (j : Fin N) : potential (cfg j) =
        2 * ⟪m0 - label, (hf j).toLp (fun z => K (cfg j) z.1)⟫_ℝ := by
      dsimp only [potential]
      rw [L2.inner_def]
      congr 1
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards [hResidual, (hf j).coeFn_toLp] with z hr hj
      simp only [Real.inner_apply, hr, hj]
    rw [hEval]
    simp_rw [hpot]
    dsimp only [mean]
    rw [real_inner_smul_right, inner_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum]
    ring
  have hPair : ((∫ q, potential q ∂rhoOf w1) - (∫ q, potential q ∂rhoOf w0)) =
      2 * ⟪m0 - label, m1 - m0⟫_ℝ := by
    rw [hPotMean w1 hf1, hPotMean w0 hf0, inner_sub_right]
    dsimp only [m0, m1]
    ring
  have hCurvePred (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (x : X) :
      predictor (curve t) x =
        (1 - t) * predictor (rhoOf w0) x + t * predictor (rhoOf w1) x := by
    dsimp only [predictor, curve]
    rw [integral_add_measure
      ((hInt w0 (fun q => K q x)).smul_measure ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top)
      ((hInt w1 (fun q => K q x)).smul_measure ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top)]
    simp only [integral_smul_measure, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (sub_nonneg.mpr ht.2),
      ENNReal.toReal_ofReal ht.1, smul_eq_mul]
  have hPredLp (cfg : Fin N → W)
      (hf : ∀ j, MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => K (cfg j) z.1) 2 P) :
      MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => predictor (rhoOf cfg) z.1) 2 P := by
    have hs := (memLp_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => hf j)).const_smul (N : ℝ)⁻¹
    exact hs.ae_eq (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun z => (hPred cfg z.1).symm))
  have hMixLp (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
      MemLp (fun z : X × ℝ => predictor (curve t) z.1 - z.2) 2 P := by
    have hs := (((hPredLp w0 hf0).const_smul (1 - t)).add
      ((hPredLp w1 hf1).const_smul t)).sub hlabel
    exact hs.ae_eq (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun z => by
      change (1 - t) * predictor (rhoOf w0) z.1 +
        t * predictor (rhoOf w1) z.1 - z.2 = predictor (curve t) z.1 - z.2
      rw [hCurvePred t ht]))
  have hMixAE (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
      (fun z => ((1 - t) • m0 + t • m1 - label) z) =ᵐ[P]
        (fun z : X × ℝ => predictor (curve t) z.1 - z.2) := by
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_sub ((1 - t) • m0 + t • m1) label,
      Lp.coeFn_add ((1 - t) • m0) (t • m1),
      Lp.coeFn_smul (1 - t) m0, Lp.coeFn_smul t m1,
      hMean w0 hf0, hMean w1 hf1, hlabel.coeFn_toLp]
      with z hsub hadd hsm0 hsm1 hm0 hm1 hy
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply, Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hsub hadd hsm0 hsm1
    rw [hsub, hadd, hsm0, hsm1, hm0, hm1, hy, hCurvePred t ht]
  have hRiskCurve (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
      risk (curve t) = ‖(1 - t) • m0 + t • m1 - label‖ ^ 2 := by
    dsimp only [risk]
    rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, L2.inner_def]
    symm
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [hMixAE t ht] with z hz
    simp only [Real.inner_apply, hz, pow_two]
  have hProps (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
      IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧
      Integrable (fun z : X × ℝ => (predictor (curve t) z.1 - z.2) ^ 2) P := by
    refine ⟨?_, (hMixLp t ht).integrable_sq⟩
    letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (rhoOf w0) := (hBase w0 hf0).1
    letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (rhoOf w1) := (hBase w1 hf1).1
    apply isProbabilityMeasure_iff.mpr
    simp only [curve, Measure.add_apply, Measure.smul_apply, measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_add (sub_nonneg.mpr ht.2) ht.1]
    norm_num
  refine ⟨hProps, hInt w0 potential, hInt w1 potential, ?_⟩
  rw [hPair]
  have hlin : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => m0 + t • (m1 - m0) - label) (m1 - m0) 0 := by
    have hs : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => t • (m1 - m0)) (m1 - m0) 0 := by
      simpa only [one_smul, id_eq] using (hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).smul_const (m1 - m0)
    exact (hs.const_add m0).sub_const label
  have hd : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => ‖m0 + t • (m1 - m0) - label‖ ^ 2)
      (2 * ⟪m0 - label, m1 - m0⟫_ℝ) 0 := by
    simpa only [zero_smul, add_zero] using hlin.norm_sq
  apply hd.hasDerivWithinAt.congr_of_mem
  · intro t ht
    rw [hRiskCurve t ht]
    congr 2
    rw [sub_smul, one_smul, smul_sub]
    abel
  · exact ⟨le_rfl, zero_le_one⟩


end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.JointEmpiricalSegmentRisk

steps.title: Use the actual finite support
steps.text: Dirac integration turns the predictor into the indexed average. Colliding particles keep their multiplicity, and every scalar function is integrable under these finite empirical laws.

steps.title: Construct genuine joint L² classes
steps.text: Pull each selected feature along the actual first-coordinate marginal. Finite sums and the supplied response class construct both endpoint means and their residual in L²(P).

steps.title: Identify the finite potential pairing
steps.text: Cauchy–Schwarz gives integrability of every required sampled residual-feature product. Finite integration yields the actual potential pairing as twice the residual inner product with the mean change.

steps.title: Identify the scalar mixture risk
steps.text: Linearity under the finite positive-measure mixture gives the actual predictor interpolation; its square is integrable and its integral equals the squared L² residual norm.

steps.title: Take the endpoint derivative
steps.text: Differentiate this affine residual norm and restrict to the probability interval. Both finite outer potential integrals already exist.
